259	### Existing system LaunchDaemons
   260	
   261	OpenClaw installs and manages a per-user LaunchAgent. It does not install or manage system LaunchDaemons. If a custom LaunchDaemon already uses the same gateway label, OpenClaw refuses to write, start, restart, or repair a user LaunchAgent because two `KeepAlive` managers can repeatedly restart the same gateway.
   262	
   263	The ownership check reads `launchctl print system/<label>` and also checks installed plists under `/Library/LaunchDaemons`. It rejects the operation when system ownership cannot be verified, and `--force` does not bypass it. `openclaw gateway status` reports a loaded same-label system job; add `--deep` to scan installed system service files.
   264	
   265	The runtime and standalone updater parse captured plist bytes with the native parser. If endpoint protection denies pathname parsing during a detached restart, its ownership scan tries a bounded read and parses the captured bytes instead. Actual permission-denied reads are skipped, while malformed data and other read failures still block activation. Loaded same-label jobs remain blocked; an unloaded same-label plist hidden by read denial cannot be detected. The detached restart fallback uses macOS's `/usr/bin/perl`; if that reader is unavailable, the scan still refuses unverifiable activation. This does not change endpoint-protection policy or suppress its alerts.

## Design priorities

- **One owner per responsibility.** Owner decides or changes authoritative state; callers consume its operations and recorded facts. Adapters translate contracts; caches and projections derive from owner with explicit invalidation lifecycle. Transports may need different adapters, never competing owners.
- **Small core, capable plugins.** Model-facing core additions cost ongoing context. Optional capability belongs at edges; core supplies generic contracts. New integration alone never warrants another core tool or manager. New capability: take the first fitting step of the [capability ladder](src/plugin-sdk/AGENTS.md#choose-the-capability-surface). [VISION.md](VISION.md) owns product scope.
- **Stable conversation context.** Generated prompt/tool/context additions: bounded, deterministic. Preserve transcript bytes; serve required instructions whole; only compaction rewrites history. Defer stable-prompt changes to next session unless owner defines explicit invalidation; keep existing skill, tool, and memory refresh contracts. Side request reusing conversation shares turn's request preparation or carries no cache identity.
=== agents AGENTS 24-32 ===
## Run Authority

- Prepare one admitted context after runtime selection; retries/fallbacks reuse it, never mint authority.
- Lifecycle owner's `finally`: close admission on terminal, error, cancellation, unsupported recovery paths.
- Harness host capabilities capture exact admitted authority. Gate tool binding/preparation/execution, hooks, approvals.
- Retained tools, preparers, callbacks, approval handles: a new call fails after close, replacement, release, abort, claim loss, lifecycle rotation. A call in progress may finish; abort stops it through its signal.
- One model resolver for every entry path (turn, `/model`, spawn, isolated/utility completions, `agent --local`, `sessions.create`): a shown model runs on each of them.
- Run on the runtime and credential the user signed in with. Fallback to API-key billing or another runtime happens only where documented, never silently.
- Native-runtime consent: asked once at provider setup by the core owner; channel chats, approvals and subagents honor it.

   265	
   266	When you replace the OpenClaw image but keep the same mounted state/config, the
   267	image entrypoint runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` under exclusive
   268	maintenance ownership before starting the Gateway. This covers the default image

10:- A single long-lived **Gateway** owns all messaging surfaces (WhatsApp via
11:  Baileys, Telegram via grammY, Slack, Discord, Signal, iMessage, WebChat).
12:- Control-plane clients (macOS app, CLI, web UI, automations) connect to the
13:  Gateway over **WebSocket** on the configured bind host (default
14:  `127.0.0.1:18789`).
15:- **Nodes** (macOS/iOS/Android/headless) also connect over **WebSocket**, but
16:  declare `role: node` with explicit caps/commands.
17:- One Gateway per host. It is the only place that opens a WhatsApp session.
--
75:## Wire protocol (summary)
76:
77:- Transport: WebSocket, text frames with JSON payloads.
78:- First frame **must** be `connect`.
79:- After handshake:
80:  - Requests: `{type:"req", id, method, params}` → `{type:"res", id, ok, payload|error}`
81:  - Events: `{type:"event", event, payload, seq?, stateVersion?}`
82:- `hello-ok.features.methods` / `events` are discovery metadata, not a
83:  generated dump of every callable helper route.
84:- Shared-secret auth accepts the configured secret in either
85:  `connect.params.auth.token` or `connect.params.auth.password`.
86:  `gateway.auth.mode` selects the configured value (`gateway.auth.token` or
87:  `gateway.auth.password`), not the required wire field.
88:- Identity-bearing modes such as Tailscale Serve
89:  (`gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true`) or non-loopback
90:  `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"` satisfy auth from request headers
91:  instead of `connect.params.auth.*`.
92:- Private-ingress `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` disables shared-secret auth
93:  entirely. Keep that mode off public or untrusted ingress.
94:- Idempotency keys are required for side-effecting methods (`send`, `agent`) to
95:  safely retry. The server keeps a short-lived dedupe cache.
96:- Nodes must include `role: "node"` plus caps/commands/permissions in `connect`.
--
98:## Pairing and local trust
99:
100:- All WS clients (operators + nodes) include a **device identity** on `connect`.
101:- New device IDs require pairing approval. The Gateway issues a **device token**
102:  for subsequent connects.
103:- Direct local loopback connects can be auto-approved to keep same-host UX
104:  smooth.
105:- OpenClaw also has a narrow backend/container-local self-connect path for
106:  trusted shared-secret helper flows.
107:- Tailnet and LAN connects, including same-host tailnet binds, still require
108:  explicit pairing approval.
109:- All connects must sign the `connect.challenge` nonce. Signature payload `v3`
110:  also binds `platform` and `deviceFamily`. The gateway pins paired metadata on
111:  reconnect and requires repair pairing for metadata changes.
112:- **Non-local** connects still require explicit approval.
113:- Gateway auth (`gateway.auth.*`) still applies to **all** connections, local or
114:  remote.
115:

170:## Invariants
171:
172:- Exactly one Gateway controls a single Baileys session per host.
173:- Handshake is mandatory. Any non-JSON or non-connect first frame is a hard close.
174:- Events are not replayed. Clients must refresh on gaps.
